chunks: The esteemed Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh al-Qummi narrated to us, my father narrated, Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi. He said:

Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq was asked about wine. He said: The Messenger of Allah said: The first things my Lord prohibited were idol worship, wine drinking, and quarrelling. God sent me as a mercy and to obliterate instruments and affairs of Jahiliyya. My Lord swore: No servant drinks wine except I give him boiling water on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Do not sit with the wine drinker, do not marry him, do not visit him in illness, do not attend his funeral. The wine drinker comes on the Day of Resurrection with darkened face, bleary eyes, slanted mouth, drooling, tongue dangling from the back of his head.

key_terms.عبادة الأوثان وشرب الخمر وملاحاة الرجال: Idol worship, drinking wine, and quarrelling with men - the three primary prohibitions
key_terms.لا تجالسوا شارب الخمر: Do not sit with the wine drinker - the commandment of social boycott
key_terms.لا يشرب عبد لي خمرا في الدنيا إلا سقيته: God's oath: no servant drinks wine in this world without drinking boiling water in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the prohibition of wine in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) relays the Prophet Muhammad's comprehensive teaching on wine: it was among the very first prohibitions God commanded, alongside idol worship and quarreling. The Prophet was sent to eradicate not just alcohol but also instruments of idle entertainment and all vestiges of pre-Islamic paganism. God swore an oath that every wine drinker would be made to drink boiling water on the Day of Resurrection. The Imam adds severe social instructions: complete social boycott of the habitual wine drinker - no companionship, no marriage ties, no visiting in illness, no attending their funeral. The hadith concludes with a vivid eschatological description of the wine drinker's appearance on Judgment Day.
